2608.20319.title: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
2608.20319.paper_summary: Naturalistic computer-use traces, passively recorded screenshots and mouse or keyboard actions, are a valuable resource for deriving symbolic, auditable, and reusable models of how everyday work is done. Such models matter as computer-use agents enter real work, where agents need to learn how tasks are actually performed, and organizations need to audit and reuse that knowledge. However, inducing such task models is challenging, as activity is observed only as low-level events and real-world work is multi-threaded with interleaved goals. Existing methods assume a given task or a single workflow, and produce step-level summaries rather than structured task models. We introduce Task Model Induction (TMI), which (i) discovers the latent tasks in an unconstrained trace, disentangling concurrent activity, and (ii) for each latent task, induces a task model pairing a hierarchical objective model of recursive goal decomposition with a procedure model of the control flow that organized the execution. Intrinsically, on controlled human and agent trajectories, TMI recovers interleaved tasks with 0.974 agreement against ground-truth groupings and reconstructs 74.9% of the observed execution steps, far more than the strongest workflow induction baseline. Extrinsically, skills derived from TMI's task models improve held-out task accuracy by 30.0% over the strongest baseline.
2608.20319.paper_summary_zh: 自然主義的電腦使用痕跡、被動記錄的截圖以及滑鼠或鍵盤操作，是推導日常工作如何進行的符號化、可審計和可重用模型的重要資源。這些模型很重要，因為電腦使用代理進入真實工作環境，代理需要學習任務實際是如何執行的，而組織需要審計並重用這些知識。然而，誘導這樣的任務模型是具有挑戰性的，因為活動僅作為低層次事件被觀察，而現實世界的工作是多線程的，且目標交錯。現有的方法假設一個給定的任務或單一的工作流程，並產生步驟級的摘要，而不是結構化的任務模型。我們介紹了任務模型誘導（TMI），它（i）在無約束的痕跡中發現潛在任務，解開並行活動，並且（ii）為每個潛在任務誘導一個任務模型，將遞歸目標分解的層次目標模型與組織執行的控制流程的程序模型配對。在受控的人類和代理軌跡上，TMI 本質上恢復了交錯任務，與真實分組的協議為 0.974，並重建了 74.9% 的觀察執行步驟，遠超過最強的工作流程誘導基準。在外部，從 TMI 的任務模型中衍生的技能使得保留任務的準確性比最強基準提高了 30.0%。
